lesson.text: Quick memory: what happens if some cleaners are mixed? (A harmful gas.) Today: carbon monoxide, and what to do in a poisoning emergency.
Carbon monoxide (CO) is a gas you can't see, smell or taste. It can come from a faulty boiler, cooker, fire or engine.
A CO alarm warns you. Grown-ups test it every month: press and hold the button until it beeps. Never take its battery out.
The CO alarm sounds: wake everyone, get out into fresh air, and call the emergency number from outside. Stay out until someone says it's safe.
Cleaning: one cleaner at a time, the window open, rinse between, read the label first. Bleach with acids or ammonia makes chlorine or chloramine gas.
A swallowed button battery or a poison: call the emergency number at once, keep the packet, and never make someone sick. Medicine: only the label's amount.
Try it in the world: open the practice house at night. Then, with a grown-up, find your CO alarm and press its test button together.

choices: a gas you can't see, smell or taste
exercises.hint: That's why it needs an alarm.
exercises.explain: A gas you can't see, smell or taste: only an alarm can warn you.

exercises.prompt: The CO alarm sounds at night. You...
exercises.explain: Wake everyone and get out into fresh air.

exercises.prompt: You should take the battery out of a CO alarm if it beeps.
exercises.explain: False: never take its battery out. Get out and call.

exercises.prompt: The CO alarm sounds: put it in order.
items: get out and call from outside
exercises.explain: Wake everyone, get out and call from outside, wait until it's safe.

exercises.prompt: How often do grown-ups test a CO alarm?
exercises.explain: Every month: press and hold the test button until it beeps.

exercises.prompt: Bleach mixed with some toilet cleaners can make a harmful gas.
exercises.explain: True: it can make chlorine gas. Use one cleaner at a time.

exercises.prompt: Someone swallowed a button battery. First...
exercises.explain: Call the emergency number at once, and never make them be sick.

exercises.prompt: Who decides how much medicine to take?
exercises.explain: The label's amount, given by a grown-up. More is never better.
One cleaner and calling from outside are safe; ignoring the alarm and mixing are not.

exercises.prompt: After a poisoning call, what do you keep to show the helpers?
exercises.hint: They need to know what it was.
exercises.explain: The bottle or the packet, so the helpers know what it was.

exercises.prompt: You can go back in as soon as the CO alarm stops.
exercises.explain: False: wait outside until the fire service or a gas engineer says it's safe.
